title: Design a test drone plane with AI agents
summary: ETH Zürich students in Project Daedalus say they designed their first test plane, Appenzell, with AI agents, then built and flew it.
agent_role: The agents helped generate, simulate and evaluate plane designs. The students built the aircraft by hand and flew it.
outcome: The team reports its first test plane was designed with AI agents, built and flown; its site lists 3 planes built, 2 flights and 3 crashes.
what_they_did: A team of eight engineering students at ETH Zürich is building a drone plane for a student design competition. They connected design generation, simulation, tuning and evaluation into one workflow with AI agents. The students then built the chosen design and flew it.
how_it_went: The poster says their first test plane, Appenzell, was designed with AI agents, built and flown. The project site lists 3 planes built, 2 flights and 3 crashes so far.
worth_knowing: The project is backed by an ETH lab focused on AI in engineering design, so the setup is not off-the-shelf. Expect crashes; the team counts three already.
prompt: Help me design a small remote-control plane for [purpose, e.g. carrying a 500 g payload]. Propose several design options with wing size, shape and weight. Estimate how each would fly using simple calculations or free simulation tools you can run. Compare the options in a table and recommend one, explaining the trade-offs. Then list the parts and build steps. Show me your reasoning before I buy any parts.

curation.rationale: A real engineering result, a student test plane designed with AI agents and flown, but the agents' exact role is only sketched. The non-coding science angle adds value despite thin detail.
